items.title: Cramer nhận thấy dấu hiệu bong bóng dot-com khi phố Wall rút khỏi cổ phiếu AI để tìm sự an toàn
items.summary:
Thời điểm hiện tại khá nhạy cảm. Seagate vừa công bố kết quả kinh doanh vượt kỳ vọng sau phiên giao dịch ngày thứ Ba. Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ cũng sẽ công bố quyết định về lãi suất trong ngày hôm nay. Cả hai sự kiện lớn này đều có thể ảnh hưởng đến nhóm cổ phiếu trung tâm dữ liệu. Trong thời gian tới, nhà đầu tư sẽ nhận thấy liệu nhóm này có ổn định trở lại, hay dòng tiền sẽ tiếp tục đổ về các cổ phiếu mà Cramer cho là “có vẻ nhàm chán nhưng an toàn”. [...] Làn sóng giảm giá mạnh nhất lại diễn ra ở thị trường châu Á. Chỉ số KOSPI Hàn Quốc đã mất hơn 10% trong tuần này. SK Hynix và Samsung Electronics đồng loạt giảm theo các đối thủ Mỹ. Những khó khăn trong chuỗi cung ứng AI đang là nguyên nhân lớn khiến thị trường rơi vào trạng thái “gấu”.

## Cramer gọi đó là sự mở rộng, không phải sụp đổ [...] Xu hướng này phản ánh trực tiếp trên bảng điện. Giá các cổ phiếu Coca-Cola, PepsiCo và Walmart đều tăng mạnh. Chỉ số Dow Jones Industrial Average tăng trong khi Nasdaq Composite lại đi xuống. Nhà quản lý quỹ Steve Eisman cũng đã chỉ ra sự phân hóa này và cảnh báo thị trường ngày nay đang vận hành như một “kèo AI” tập trung duy nhất.

items.title: Why Continuous Hormone Monitoring Could Transform Women's Health Monitoring - Forbes
items.summary: # Ida Tin Coined Femtech. Now She’s Funding Continuous Hormone Monitoring. Ida Tin coined "femtech" and built Clue. Now she's directing a €40 million German government challenge to fund what femtech skipped: biosensors that read hormones continuously in real time. The goal isn't a single winning product—it's the shared scientific infrastructure, including the first standardized hormone dataset, that no startup could build alone. A jury convened in Leipzig and selected the eight teams to compete for the €40 million SPRIND Continuous Hormone Monitoring Challenge in Europe’s first government-backed race to develop biosensors that measure at least four hormones over seven days. Leading the effort is Ida Tin, the Danish entrepreneur who founded the period-tracking app, Clue, in 2012 and coined the term “femtech” in 2016—a word that helped make women’s health a recognized investment category. That gap, she argues, explains why a decade of femtech investment has not materially closed the diagnostic divide for the most common women’s health conditions.

items.title: Yujin Technology Selected for Government AI Manufacturing Platform Project - thelec.net
items.summary: * UPDATE : 2026-07-22 21:26 (Wed). Yujin Technology Selected for Government AI Manufacturing Platform Project. ## Consortium to develop generative AI platform for battery equipment manufacturing with 1.1 billion won in first-year funding. * Published 2026.07.22 21:26. Yujin Technology said on July 22 that it has been selected as the preferred bidder for the South Korean government's 2026 AI Transformation (AX) One-Stop Voucher Program, led by the Ministry of Science and ICT and the National IT Industry Promotion Agency (NIPA). Yujin Technology will carry out the project through a consortium with Plan I and Gabia, developing a generative AI-based manufacturing platform for battery equipment. The project will receive approximately 1.1 billion won in government funding during its first year. A second year of funding of a similar scale is expected following an evaluation of the first year's performance. During the first phase, Yujin Technology plans to complete development of the AI platform and conduct proof-of-concept demonstrations.

items.summary:
The letter comes on the heels of major advancements and burgeoning threats from rapidly developing AI systems. OpenAI disclosed last week that two of its test models escaped a lab environment, bypassed its systems to gain access to the open internet and hacked a different company’s internal system. [...] “We’re glad to see broad agreement across the field on the need for technical and governance tools to pace the frontier of AI development, including the ability to slow it, so society can prepare,” Anthropic said in a comment to CNN.

Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis also recently called for a new international standards body to help set protocols for new AI models, an idea endorsed by Altman, SpaceX’s Elon Musk, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and other major industry figures. [...] OpenAI said in a statement to CNN they agree with potentially pacing the development of AI, adding they “hope to contribute to work led by the U.S. government, alongside other labs” on the topic.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggested it may be time to slow down AI development in a podcast interview Tuesday. The OpenAI models that broke out of their test environment are fueling “long term questions” about how AI companies should address this new rate of progress.

The administration's AI Action Plan directs the Department of Labor to prioritize AI skill development across workforce funding streams and proposes an AI Workforce Research Hub. Beginning July 1, students became eligible for Pell Grants covering short-term programs in high-skill, in-demand fields. [...] ## The Bottom Line

Eight hearings in, the committee has built a case for AI as an opportunity engine without producing legislation that reconciles it with what Barlow and McBath described. Access the Legis1 platform for comprehensive political news, data, and insights. [...] ## What's Next

Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) introduced the AI Workforce Training Act in February, creating a 30 percent tax credit for employer-provided AI training. Sen. Jim Banks (R-IN) introduced the AI Workforce PREPARE Act in December 2025, which would establish an Artificial Intelligence Workforce Research Hub at the Department of Labor and require employers to disclose when AI was a substantial factor in a mass layoff. Both remain in committee.

Reports and Proceedings [...] A new system developed by MIT computer scientists helps robots operate much faster.
 The method doubled the speed of robots performing activities like pick-and-place tasks, while significantly reducing lag time between motions.

items.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model—and What ...
items.summary:
OpenAI was evaluating its artificial intelligence models’ ability to exploit vulnerable software when instead the models hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, broke containment, and attacked a real company, OpenAI revealed on July 21. Observers say this is the first real-world instance of AI doing something researchers have long worried about: a loss-of-control scenario. If the industry fails to learn from it, it is unlikely to be the last. [...] OpenAI did not respond to TIME’s request for comment, but has said it has partnered with Hugging Face to conduct a thorough investigation and will share more details once complete. But perhaps more worryingly, OpenAI is not legally compelled to disclose the incident in the first place. [...] # What happened?

On July 16, Hugging Face said it had been hit by an unusually automated cyberattack. Over the course of a weekend, AI agents carried out thousands of actions across many temporary virtual computers, moving through the company’s internal systems and shifting the infrastructure coordinating the attack between online services to keep it running. Five days later, OpenAI disclosed that its own models were responsible.
